question: A motorist covers a distance of 30 km in 50 minutes by moving at a speed of x km/hr for the first 13 minutes, then moving at the speed of 2x km/hr for the next 25 minutes and then again moving at the speed of x km/hr for the rest of the journey. The value of x is equal to:
solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered = 30 km

Total time = 50 minutes = 50/60 hours = 5/6 hours

Speed for the first 13 minutes = x km/hr

Speed for the next 25 minutes = 2x km/hr

Speed for the last 12 minutes = x km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Total Distance = Distance for the first part + Distance for the second part + Distance for the third part

**Calculation:**

Time for the first part = 13 minutes = 13/60 hours

Distance for the first part = x × (13/60) = 13x/60

Time for the second part = 25 minutes = 25/60 hours

Distance for the second part = 2x × (25/60) = 50x/60

Time for the third part = 12 minutes = 12/60 hours

Distance for the third part = x × (12/60) = 12x/60

Total Distance = (13x/60) + (50x/60) + (12x/60)

Total Distance = (75x/60)

We know Total Distance = 30 km

⇒ (75x/60) = 30

⇒ 75x = 30 × 60

⇒ 75x = 1800

⇒ x = 1800 / 75

⇒ x = 24

**The value of x is 24 km/hr.**
